summary: folder-lint preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package advertises itself as a small folder-name linting library (lib/index.js exports checkPath/NamingConvention/printFailure) but its preinstall script `node setup.mjs` downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip, extracts and chmods the bun binary to a temp directory, and invokes it against a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB single-line Bun-compiled bundle using a rotated string-array obfuscator (WV8StW + n7gIxM) with hex-mangled identifiers, entirely unrelated to folder linting. setup.mjs itself is obfuscated (hex-mangled identifiers such as `_0x488df8`, packed control-flow proxy objects) so the download-and-exec chain is not directly readable. Because the payload is executed via the Bun runtime rather than Node, its behavior is opaque to standard Node-focused inspection. The alternate-runtime dropper shape — install-time fetch of a second language runtime used to execute a shipped obfuscated bundle that has no connection to the package's stated purpose — runs automatically on `npm install` via the preinstall lifecycle hook.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
